title: I Recorded the Loading-Dock Appointment After They Waved a Cousin's Truck

parts.text: I had dock 2 from 2:00 to 2:30 and at 2:04 a unmarked van rolled in on a wave from supervisor Len. The board said: APPOINTMENT ON THE BOARD. THIRTY MINUTES. NO WAVES. I was forty-three, driver, holding a printed window. Len did not unwave. "Family is freight." I photographed the board, the window, and the van on my dock. Then I logged a wave. At 2:12 dispatch asked why Len's van was on dock 2 without a line. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Dispatch can see an unmarked van on dock 2 with no board line during my window.

social.video_title: He waved a cousin's van onto my appointment — Part 1/2
social.description: Loading dock, a printed window, and a wave. I logged it. Would you have photographed the van?

parts.text: Len called it a hot load until dispatch asked for the log. I printed the wave, the photo, and the board. The van left. Len booked freight like freight and told the yard hot was always about optics. Optics is a word supervisors use when a van exists. Appointment now has a second line: FAMILY IS NOT A WAVE. I keep my thirty. Len boards. The dock finally looks like a window, not a reunion. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Family is not a wave — Part 2/2
social.description: Wave log, cleared dock, and a second line. Was a hot load ever no line?
